People are told to worship their Lord, who created them, made the earth a bed and the sky a ceiling, and sent rain, and not to attribute equals to Allah.
Some take equals besides Allah and love them as Allah, but when they see the punishment, leaders and followers disown one another, and they will never leave the Fire.
Allah will cast terror into the disbelievers' hearts for associating with Him what He gave no authority for, and their refuge is the Fire.
Allah does not forgive association with Him but forgives anything less for whom He wills; associating others with Him is a tremendous sin.
Allah does not forgive association with Him; those who associate have strayed far, calling on female deities and, in truth, on a rebellious Satan.
People are asked why they worship besides Allah what cannot harm or benefit them, and the People of the Scripture are told not to exceed limits in religion.
On the Day of gathering the polytheists will be asked where their claimed partners are, and they will swear they never associated others, lying about themselves.
The polytheists assign shares of crops and livestock to their partners, kill their children, and forbid animals by their own claim, inventing lies about Allah, and so have lost.
The polytheists will say that had Allah willed they would not have associated; they follow assumption, and if they bring witnesses to their bans, do not testify with them.
Allah created people from one soul and its mate; a couple who prayed for a good child ascribe partners to Him in what He gave them.
The Prophet and believers are not to ask forgiveness for polytheists, even relatives, once clearly for Hellfire; Abraham disassociated from his father once he saw him as Allah's enemy.
They worship besides Allah what neither harms nor benefits them, calling these their intercessors, as if informing Allah of something He does not know.
Do not doubt what these people worship; they worship only as their fathers worshipped before, and they will be given their share in full.
People pass by the signs in the heavens and earth, and most believe in Allah only while associating others; the Prophet invites to Allah with insight and associates none.
Allah maintains every soul, yet they attribute partners to Him; challenged to name them, they are averted from the way, and none guides whom Allah leaves astray.
Declare what is commanded and turn away from the polytheists; Allah suffices against the mockers who make another deity with Him, and they will come to know.
He who creates is not like one who does not; Allah's favors are countless, and those invoked besides Him create nothing, are created, and are dead.
People cry to Allah in hardship, yet once it is lifted some associate others with Him and give a share of His provision to what they do not know.
Those favored in provision would not share it equally with those their right hands possess; Allah gave spouses, children and provision, yet they worship what provides nothing.
Do not set up another deity with Allah, or you will be censured and forsaken.
This is wisdom revealed to the Prophet: set up no other deity with Allah, and do not claim He gave you sons and took the angels as daughters.
Those invoked besides Allah cannot remove harm; they themselves seek a way to their Lord, hoping for His mercy and fearing His punishment.
Those taken as allies besides Allah did not witness the creation of the heavens and earth or of themselves, and He would not take misguiders as assistants.
They take gods besides Allah for honor, but those gods will deny their worship and turn against them.
No one protects them from the Most Merciful, and their gods cannot help themselves; long given good things, they ignore warnings, yet a whiff of punishment makes them confess wrongdoing.
Invoking instead of Allah what neither harms nor benefits is extreme error, and what is invoked has harm closer than its benefit, a wretched protector and associate.
Honoring Allah's sacred ordinances is best; livestock is permitted except what is recited, idols and false statements must be avoided, and associating with Allah is like falling from the sky.
They worship besides Allah that for which He sent no authority and of which they have no knowledge, and the wrongdoers will have no helper.
Those invoked besides Allah could never create a fly even together, nor recover what a fly takes from them; people have not appraised Allah as He deserves.
They worship besides Allah what neither benefits nor harms them, and the disbeliever is ever an assistant against his Lord.
Do not invoke another deity with Allah and so be among the punished.
Those taking allies other than Allah are like the spider whose home is weakest; Allah knows what they call upon, and only those of knowledge understand such examples.
At sea they supplicate Allah sincerely, but once delivered to land they associate others with Him, denying what He granted and enjoying themselves.
Allah gives an example from people themselves, asking whether they would make those their right hands possess equal partners in their provision, fearing them as each other.
People call on their Lord in hardship, but once He lets them taste mercy some associate others with Him, and they are asked what revealed authority supports this.
Allah merges night and day, runs the sun and moon; those invoked besides Him own not a date seed's membrane, cannot answer, and will deny that worship on Resurrection Day.
Those who invoke partners are asked what those partners created on earth, what share they hold in the heavens, or what scripture backs them; the wrongdoers promise only delusion.
They took deities besides Allah hoping for help, but these cannot help them; the Prophet should not grieve at their words, for Allah knows what they hide and show.
Told there is no deity but Allah, they arrogantly asked whether to leave their gods for a mad poet, though the Prophet brought truth; they will taste painful punishment.
Disbelievers call the warner a lying magician who made the gods one God, urge patience over their gods and doubt the message, yet own no dominion and will be defeated.
Allah's example of a slave owned by quarreling partners and one belonging to a single man shows they are not equal, though most people do not know.
Intercession belongs entirely to Allah, not to powerless intercessors people take, yet deniers of the Hereafter shrink at Allah's name alone and rejoice when others are mentioned.
The Prophet refuses to worship other than Allah, for he and those before were told associating partners voids one's work, and he is to worship Allah alone and be grateful.
The Prophet is only a man to whom it is revealed that God is one; woe to those who associate others with Allah, give no zakah and deny the Hereafter.
Allah is Guardian over those who take allies other than Him, and the Prophet is not their manager.
Those who take protectors besides Allah are told that Allah is the Protector, who gives life to the dead and is competent over all things.
They are asked whether other deities ordained for them a religion Allah did not consent to; but for the decisive word it would be settled, and wrongdoers face painful punishment.
They assign Allah daughters, leaving sons for themselves, grieve at such news, call the angels females, and claim Allah willed their worship, without knowledge.
Worshippers are challenged to show anything their invoked partners created; these will not answer them until the Day of Resurrection, then become their enemies and deny their worship.
Al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat are mere names without authority from Allah, an unjust division giving Him females; those who named them follow assumption and desire, though guidance came.
